source.title: Fast Escape, Slow Convergence: Learning Dynamics of Phase Retrieval under Power-Law Data
source.authors: Guillaume Braun; Bruno Loureiro; Ha Quang Minh; Masaaki Imaizumi

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendix are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Studies scaling behavior in anisotropic phase retrieval, a nonlinear regression setting beyond text pretraining, and reports theoretical and numerical results for MSE over training time.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as background but does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute, compute-optimal allocation, architecture sensitivity, or downstream-task predictability. Its relevant results concern phase-retrieval MSE under a power-law input spectrum and training time.
record.test_reason: This is a theory paper on gradient-flow phase retrieval (a single quadratic neuron) with power-law Gaussian inputs. It derives MSE-versus-training-time curves governed by the input spectral exponent a. No row measures held-out loss of a trained model against parameters, tokens or compute, in any modality or regime V5 names. It does not test extrapolation, allocation, shape or downstream performance either. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation. The results describe a related but different construct: training-time error dynamics of a toy model under an assumed data spectrum. They are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests of V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors derive a three-phase gradient-flow trajectory for anisotropic phase retrieval. After a plateau up to T2, MSE decays at a rate controlled by the spectral tail, with the exponent a setting the log–log slope. Online SGD shows the same phases qualitatively. The quantitative results hold only for Gaussian inputs in the gradient-flow limit; extending them to discrete-time SGD remains open.
record.recipe_differences: This is a theoretical and numerical study of population gradient flow in nonlinear phase retrieval with anisotropic Gaussian inputs, not a language-model scaling sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The spectral exponent a changes the reported convergence behavior; larger a is associated with slower MSE decay. The analysis is for gradient flow, while online-SGD simulations are reported qualitatively.

fits_no_version.finding: Under gradient flow, anisotropic phase retrieval with spectrum λi ∝ i^-a goes through three phases: fast escape, slow convergence of summary statistics, and spectral-tail learning. The MSE plateaus until T2, then decays at a rate set by a, including a window where 1 − Sd scales as τ^(1/a)/d. Numerical checks (Figures 1, 4–6) agree qualitatively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In nonlinear single-index regression with power-law input spectra, the training-time error curve follows explicit power-law or plateau regimes whose exponents are set by the spectral decay.

record.problems: The quantitative theory is limited to Gaussian inputs with a power-law spectrum and the gradient-flow limit. Numerical experiments are limited, and the online-SGD results are described as qualitative; the paper says extending the quantitative results to discrete-time SGD remains open.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 reports MSE and summary-statistic trajectories, but the relevant MSE evidence is represented by the theorem-based rows and Figure 1. Figures 3–6 report correlation or order-parameter dynamics, approximation checks, or qualitative SGD behavior rather than additional separately quantified MSE scaling outcomes.

untested.parts: No language-model loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No trained models in other modalities or regimes (image, video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer); the only system is a theoretical phase-retrieval model.
No comparison of fitting choices or of published exponents.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's guess (tests, T3, V5 supports/limits_scope) is rejected. The study is a toy theoretical model of training-time dynamics, not a test of the LM scaling-law versions. It is not one of the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small language-model runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.

Tests only anisotropic phase retrieval with Gaussian inputs and a power-law spectrum; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or whether the same held-out cross-entropy law applies.
No comparison of fitting choices or evidence about disagreement between published language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits.

tranche.reason: The results concern signal-recovery MSE versus training time in a single quadratic neuron and its spectral proxy. They do not test the loss, allocation, architecture, extrapolation or downstream-performance claims in the listed versions.
